# housesitter

> Keeps an always-on Mac that hosts AI agents alive and drivable, hands-off, through a cheap IP-KVM (GL.iNet Comet / any PiKVM-API KVM). A sitter on the KVM unlocks FileVault after a panic (typing a sealed copy of the password only at the prompt), power-cycles a hang through a smart plug, and messages you once when stuck. Agents get screenshot/click/type/key on the Mac from before login, in Anthropic computer-use shape, over Tailscale, LAN or a GitHub gist outbox.

## Start
- [README](README.md): what it does, quickstart, status
- `housesitter demo`: a rehearsed night, no hardware
- `housesitter adopt <mac> --fake`: arrival day, rehearsed

## For agents driving a Mac
- `housesitter ls <mac>` then `housesitter do <mac> <action> '<json>'` (Ouro Reins shape; refusals action-unavailable / input-invalid / action-failed; exit 0 ok, 2 refused, 1 failed)
- `housesitter computer <mac> '{"action":"left_click","coordinate":[x,y]}'` (Anthropic computer-use input as-is)
- To drive the app windows themselves (the accessibility tree, with this KVM's pixels as the fallback), use [hackamore](https://github.com/ourostack/hackamore): `hackamore ls <app> --kvm <mac>`.
- Library: `import { open } from '@ouro.bot/housesitter'` → `screenshot/click/type/key/scroll/computer`
- Coordinates are in the last screenshot's pixels.
- Never type a password; `type` refuses anything that looks like one. Ask the sitter: `housesitter unlock <mac>` at FileVault or the lock screen; at any other password prompt, the sitter's `type_secret` op (the plugin's `sitter_type_secret` tool, or `sitter.py do type_secret '{"name":"setup-password","prompt":"sudo in Terminal","enter":true,"seen":"<result.frame of the screenshot you judged>"}'` over SSH; never the outbox; only if a fresh picture still matches that frame and it is under 30 s old) types its own sealed copy of a named secret, 20 an hour, audited without the value. Seal one on the KVM with `housesitter secret <mac> <name> --kvm`.
- Mac locked and you need its UI? `housesitter want-desktop <mac> [--minutes 10]` (or the Reins action `want_desktop`): the sitter unlocks it through its own gates, only if its config says `"unlock_lock_screen": "on_request"` or `true`; otherwise action-unavailable.
- Smart plug: `housesitter plug <mac> find|adopt [ip]|status|prove --attended`.
- Deploy a tool's release: `housesitter deploy housesitter|shepherd [--ref <tag|branch|sha>] [--dry-run] [--json] --why "…"` builds and checks the release, then swaps `current` in one rename; jobs run from `current`. Never `git pull` in a live clone.
- Health probe: config `health` is `{host, port}` (TCP) or `{kind: "json_age", url, field, max_age_min}` (a heartbeat JSON; fresh = up, unreachable = unknown).
- Fleet view: `housesitter fleet [--stale-min 15] [--disk-floor-gb 20] [--always-on <mac>,<mac>] [--from <gist.json>]` reads the Macs' health records from the fleet gist (`HOUSESITTER_FLEET_GIST`, read with `HOUSESITTER_FLEET_USER`'s gh token) and prints one row per Mac with how old its record is and what is wrong; exit 1 when anything is.
- Copilot app restart: `housesitter restart-copilot --resume [--dry-run|--detach|--status] [--why "…"] [--also <session id>] [--skip <session id>]` (skips also come from `~/.config/housesitter/restart-copilot.json` `{ "skip": [...] }`; a session idle for over 24 h is never resumed) asks working sessions to reach a safe point, quits the app through hackamore's Quit menu item, relaunches it (SIGKILL to stragglers that outlive SIGTERM, a retried relaunch, a window opened if the app came up without one, and one message to the agent only if it still cannot come back), resumes every session that was working and checks each took a turn (exit 0 all resumed, 1 failed, 2 refused). `--app "<name>"` rehearses the sequence on another app. `--status` reports the run now or the last (state, step, start, result; exit 0 when it could be read, a failed restart is in the text and in `--json`; a session archived on purpose is listed as "archived, not resumed" and is not a failure). `--resume-only [--watch [--open-at-login]]` resumes what a crash, update or login left unfinished, and `--install-keeper` loads the launchd agent that does it for every new app process.
- Copilot app freeze and crash recovery: `housesitter restart-copilot --heartbeat` (launchd, every 30 s, no model turns) probes the app's socket and window; failing for 2 minutes is a freeze: it samples the app, SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs the exact pids, relaunches, resumes the working sessions and tells the agent once. Shepherd's `shepherd watch` (every minute, no model turns) follows every resumed session for six hours, asks again once, and tells the agent by name only about what stays broken; `shepherd watch --status` shows it, and `restart-copilot --status` shows the heartbeat and incidents. `--os-updates` (every 5 min, no admin rights) leaves the install to macOS (automatic install, or a deadline the device's management enforces) and coordinates around it: shortly before macOS acts it gets every working session to a safe point, arms the Apple Account prompt (`apple-account --expect-reboot`) and holds for the reboot, then stands down if the Mac did not restart; with automatic install off it tells the agent once which setting a person must turn on; `--now` runs the safe point at once. `--install-recovery [--mac <mac>]` loads them all.
- Mutual watch: `housesitter watch-kvm <mac> --install` on the Mac: a LaunchAgent that asks the sitter for its status every minute over SSH (`do watch_check`), or, when SSH can't reach the KVM and an outbox is configured, from the outbox gist (`ok via outbox` in its log), and sends one message after 5 min of silence and one when it's back, sharing the sitter's daily email cap. `doctor` shows "watched by the Mac itself".
- Launchd jobs kept off: config `launchd_disabled: ["<label>", …]`; `housesitter hold [--dry-run|--json|--quiet] [--why "…"]` disables each again if it came back on and stops a running one by PID. `bot.ouro.housesitter.hold` runs it hourly (launchd, no model turns, output to its log only).
- Messages: ntfy or a webhook; `adopt --notify ntfy --email <address>` also emails one address through an ntfy.sh account (token: `housesitter secret <mac> ntfy-token`; 5 emails a day on a free account). `housesitter alert-test <mac>` sends one real stuck message marked TEST.

## Housesitter, the agent on the KVM
- [plugins/housesitter](plugins/housesitter/README.md): an Ouro plugin. MCP tools sitter_status, sitter_look, sitter_screenshot, sitter_unlock, sitter_want_desktop, sitter_power_cycle, sitter_power_on, sitter_click, sitter_type, sitter_type_secret, sitter_key, sitter_scroll (each runs `sitter.py do <op>` and returns its reply as is), peer_send, peer_inbox, kvm_health; watch.py wakes the agent with `ouro msg --to <agent>`; skills/housesitter/SKILL.md.
- Peer link with the agent on the Mac: `housesitter peer send <text> [--re <id>] [--now]`, `housesitter peer inbox [--peek]`, `housesitter peer flush [--now]`, `housesitter peer watch [--agent ouroboros] [--every 30] [--once]` (wakes the agent with `ouro msg` on new messages without marking them read, and flushes what's due). Free text, one gist file per message; sends are queued and flushed in one PATCH at most every 6 minutes (`--now`/`now` at once), at most 10 gist writes an hour each way (HOUSESITTER_PEER_FLUSH_SEC, HOUSESITTER_PEER_MAX_PER_HOUR).

## Code
- src/watchdog.mjs and device/sitter.py: the same rules, both tested against spec/watchdog-cases.json
- src/hands.mjs: the pixel driver and transports
- src/adopt.mjs: arrival day
- device/sitter.py: the always-on watcher on the KVM (Python 3 standard library only)
- src/copilot-app.mjs: restart-copilot's steps (ask, quit through hackamore, relaunch, resume, verify); the peer watch reads its status.json
- The house and the flock: Housesitter keeps the Mac, the app as a running process, and the launchd jobs listed under `launchd_disabled` in its config off; the app's sessions are [Shepherd](https://github.com/ourostack/shepherd)'s, and Housesitter calls its library for safe points, progress and resume messages.
- src/peer.mjs and plugins/housesitter/peer.py: the two ends of the peer link; src/peer-watch.mjs: the Mac's watcher
